messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo performance recap: SLO checklist & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya 

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap of the performance topics we covered and the open items we agreed to confirm: 

1) Latency targets 
   - Goal: P95 <= 250ms for single-turn generation (avg input length ~150 tokens).
2) Throughput expectations 
   - Baseline: 100 reqs/min steady-state for the pilot; peak burst to 400 reqs/min for scheduled batch jobs.
3) Concurrency 
   - Concurrent active sessions: target 50 concurrent streams for the event flow.
4) Streaming requirements 
   - Need server-side streaming with <100ms first-byte for user-perceived realtime.
5) Fallback policy 
   - If model variant unavailable, route to smaller quantized variant with predictable latency.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Share an SLO checklist and a MAP (mutual action plan) with technical prescriptive items (attached).
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra/engineering team to align on load profile and network egress rules.

Can you confirm the latency/throughput numbers above or call out adjustments? Also please share the engineering contacts you want on the deep-dive.

Thanks 
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0132

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo performance recap: SLO checklist & next steps

Thanks Marissa  great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: P95 <= 250ms sounds reasonable for the single-turn path. For interactive chat (multi-turn) we may accept P95 <= 400ms if the model quality tradeoff is significant.
- Throughput: 100 reqs/min baseline is our expected steady performance for the pilot. The 400 reqs/min burst is accurate for payroll peak windows.
- Concurrency: 50 concurrent streams is optimistic but achievable if we have efficient batching; can Redwood's runtime guarantee <300ms P95 at that concurrency for our average payload?
- Streaming: First-byte <100ms is a hard requirement for our UX. If streaming warmup is needed, we'd like that to be covered in the MAP.

We can join a technical deep-dive. Engineers: Priya Shah (platform lead) and I will attend. Please include an expected runbook for load tests and any egress/CORS requirements.

-Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, FinTechCo

Alex  appreciate the specifics. Quick answers and attachments included: 

- Concurrency guarantee: Our Dedicated and Private runtimes can meet P95 <= 300ms at 50 concurrent streams for the model family we demoed (gptx-13b-quant). We'll include the benchmark matrix in the attached checklist.
- Streaming warmup: MAP item #3 covers prefix caching and cold-start mitigation; we recommend a short pre-warm job during your nightly window (we include the runbook).
- Load tests: we'll provide a k6 script and expected token-length distributions; Aditya will run an initial soak from our staging to validate.

Attachments: FinTechCo_SLO_Checklist.xlsx (detailed SLO matrix, test artifacts)
